findings.evidence: Line 57: private `commutator_mem_higher_roots` already takes `[(t.rationalRootSystem ht).IsNotG2]`; line 191-192: `have : (t.rationalRootSystem ht).IsNotG2 := by obtain ⟨n, rfl | rfl⟩ := hBC <;> infer_instance` is the only use of `hBC`; `PositiveCombinations.lean:36` lemmas need only `[P.IsNotG2]`.
findings.fix: Replace `hBC` with `[(t.rationalRootSystem ht).IsNotG2]` in both theorems, drop the `_of_typeBC` suffix, and rename the module (e.g. `Collection/NotG2.lean`). B/C then follow from the new instances.
findings.issue: `commutator_range_chevalleyRootSubgroup_le_of_typeBC` and `mem_iSup_positive_root_ranges_iff_of_typeBC` (line 199) assume `hBC : ∃ n, t = B n ∨ t = C n`, used only at line 191 to synthesize `IsNotG2`. The proof works for every non-G₂ type (A, D, E, F₄), so the open per-type collection PRs would have to repeat it.

findings.evidence: Lines 30-42 and 46-58 are identical except for the B/C-specific lemma names.
findings.fix: Prove once `isNotG2_rationalRootSystem_of_abs_pairing_le_two (h : ∀ i j, |(t.simplyConnectedRootDatum ht).pairing i j| ≤ 2) : (t.rationalRootSystem ht).IsNotG2`, and derive each instance in one line.
findings.issue: `instIsNotG2RationalRootSystemB` and `instIsNotG2RationalRootSystemC` repeat the same proof, differing only in the rewrite lemma `simplyConnectedRootDatum_B/C` and the bound lemma.

summary: The public collection theorems are restricted to types B/C, but the B/C hypothesis is used only to obtain `IsNotG2`, which the private core lemma already takes as its assumption, so the result is under-generalized. The two `IsNotG2` instances also duplicate one proof that should be a general lemma.
